title: CAP Theorem Explained
description: Understand the foundational CAP theorem and what it means for designing distributed systems.

data.text: The CAP theorem, proposed by Eric Brewer, states that a distributed data store can simultaneously guarantee only two of the following three properties: Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance. Consistency means every read returns the most recent write. Availability means every request receives a non-error response. Partition tolerance means the system continues operating despite network partitions between nodes. Because network failures are inevitable, real distributed systems must choose between consistency and availability when partitions occur.

During a partition, nodes lose the ability to communicate. If the system prioritizes consistency, it must reject some requests to prevent stale reads. If it prioritizes availability, it may return outdated data. Since a partition is unavoidable in wide-area networks, partition tolerance becomes mandatory for modern web systems, leaving architects to choose between consistency and availability.

data.title: Real-World Reality
data.text: CAP is often oversimplified. In practice, systems make fine-grained trade-offs rather than a single binary choice for every operation. Timeouts, conflict resolution, and quorum mechanisms let engineers tune the boundary between consistency and availability.

rows: Reject writes or reads to preserve consistency
Accept writes and reads, risking stale data
Impossible under partition; works only when no partition occurs

items.question: Does CAP mean I can never have all three?
items.answer: Yes, under a partition. When no partition occurs, a system can temporarily satisfy all three. The theorem is specifically about the trade-off during partitions.

items.question: Is CAP still relevant for modern cloud systems?
items.answer: Absolutely. CAP defines the design space for every distributed database, message queue, and consensus algorithm you will encounter.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: CAP applies specifically during network partitions.
Partition tolerance is mandatory for geographically distributed systems.
The real choice is between consistency and availability when a partition occurs.
CP systems reject requests to stay consistent; AP systems accept requests and repair conflicts later.
data.takeaway: CAP is a guide, not a law. It frames the design space so you can explain why your system makes the choices it does.
